answer.why: As an insider, 'Confirmed & Substantive' made me laugh straight away. It is exactly the phrase you hear when someone finally gets their appointment made permanent, and it signals the makers know the real texture of the service rather than just the headline. 'Minister Salary' is the title any outsider would reach for, and it reads like a clickbait jab at a topic Singaporeans have been arguing about for years. I would tap the first out of recognition and the second only out of mild irritation.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical or cynical game about the pay debate: chasing the big benchmarked salary, maybe a lot of jokes about the million-dollar figure. I would worry it gets the details wrong, or that it is a meme game with a political slant, and I would be braced to wince at wrong grades and titles. It does not tell me the game is about the daily grind of a career, though the store page would help.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A quieter, drier, more insider game about the actual career ladder: acting appointments, waiting to be confirmed, the paperwork of promotion and the slow grind of appraisal cycles. It sounds like someone who has actually worked in the service wrote it. The risk is that it is too obscure for outsiders, and the ampersand makes it sound a bit like a law firm, but I would be curious enough to try it.

best_moment.what: Critiquing the young AO and teaching him, then seeing him become my Deputy Secretary and thank me. It felt like how real mentoring pays off slowly and quietly.

worst_moment.what: The Telegram leak with eleven on the list, ending in an inconclusive inquiry. It was a lot of reading with no resolution, and the strained eleven never really came back.

answer.held_back_by: Low REP. I was candid and put others first, which the game treated as admirable but not popular, and it cost me with voters. In the real service that would be about right: integrity gets you trusted, not necessarily liked.
answer.ending_fair_why: Losing at 48.2% in a GRC after a REP of 54 is plausible, and the card said it was never about me, which is true to how team-slate contests work. But I would have liked to see the unopened folder pay off.
answer.chase_next: The politics route with a higher REP, to see whether I can win the ward and what a minister's life is like. I never saw the Minister part, and that is what the title promises.
answer.play_again_why: I want to see the other branch, but I would wait. The middle years were repetitive, and several threads (folder, the nine) were left hanging.

answer.title_fit_why: The game was most alive in the grades, appraisals, mentoring and quiet nominations. The salary and politics side was thin, and I retired as a Perm Sec without ever being a minister.
